This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement  (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2.
Heard learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner and learned counsel appearing for the State-Opposite Party.
Perused the materials placed before this Court.

3. The present bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the Petitioner for regular bail in connection with C.T. Case No.220 of 2023, arising out of Byree P.S. Case No.32 of 2023, pending in the Court of learned J.M.F.C., Chandikhol for alleged commission of offences punishable under Sections 294/ 341/ 323/ 376(2)(n)/ 506/34 of the I.P.C.
4.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the Petitioner is in custody since 13.02.2023.

He further contended that the investigation of the case has substantially // 2 //
progressed.
He also contended that the Petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.

In support of his contention, learned counsel for the Petitioner referred to the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. and on perusal of the statement of the victim under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., it appears that the same has been recorded on 13.2.2023 wherein she has stated that she had consensual relationship with the present Petitioner.
Thereafter, some of the photos were taken of their intimate relationship and were there in the memory chip of mobile phone of the accused.
Later on such photographs were sent to the brother-in-law of the victim.
Therefore, the Informant lodged the F.I.R. before the police station.
In the intervention of the IIC of the concerned police station, such photographs have been deleted from the mobile phone of the accused.

sentences.text: Accordingly, she has stated that the matter has been compromised.
Further, it has been stated that then the accused abused the victim in filthy language in January, 2023.
Out of anger, the Informant has lodged the F.I.R.
She has also stated that she does not have any relationship with the Petitioner at the moment and she is interested to settle the matter.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the Informant filed an affidavit stating therein that the Informant does not have any objection, if the Petitioner be released on bail.

Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, opposed the release of the Petitioner on bail on the ground that the allegations made against the Petitioner is serious in nature and the investigation of the case is going on.
Accordingly, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the State that the Petitioner should not be released on bail at this stage.

7. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels for the respective parties and upon conspectus of the surrounding facts and circumstances of the present case and taking into consideration the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. as well as the statement made by the learned counsel for the Informant, this Court is inclined to release the Petitioner on bail subject to certain terms and conditions.
8.

Hence, it is directed that the Petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing bail bond of Rs.30,000/-(Rupees thirty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court in seisin over the matter.
Violation of any of the terms and conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
9. With the aforesaid observation and direction, the BLAPL is disposed of.
